options.label: A
options.text: It allows directly connected neighbors to share configuration information

options.label: B
options.text: It reduces routing failures by allowing Layer 3 load balancing between OSPF neighbors that have the same link metric

prompt: An engineer is configuring NAT to translate the source subnet of 10.10.0.0/24 to any one of three addresses: 192.168.3.1, 192.168.3.2, or 192.168.3.3. Which configuration should be used?

options.label: A
options.text: enable configure terminal ip nat pool mypool 192.168.3.1 192.168.3.3 prefix-length 30 access-list 1 permit 10.10.0.0 0.0.0.255 ip nat outside destination list 1 pool mypool interface g1/1 ip nat inside interface g1/2 ip nat outside

options.label: B
options.text: enable configure terminal ip nat pool mypool 192.168.3.1 192.168.3.3 prefix-length 30 access-list 1 permit 10.10.0.0 0.0.0.254 ip nat inside source list 1 pool mypool interface g1/1 ip nat inside interface g1/2 ip nat outside

options.label: C
options.text: enable configure terminal ip nat pool mypool 192.168.3.1 192.168.3.3 prefix-length 30 route map permit 10.10.0.0 255.255.255.0 ip nat outside destination list 1 pool mypool interface g1/1 ip nat inside interface g1/2 ip nat outside

options.label: D
options.text: enable configure terminal ip nat pool mypool 192.168.3.1 192.168.3.3 prefix-length 30 access-list 1 permit 10.10.0.0 0.0.0.255 ip nat inside source list 1 pool mypool interface g1/1 ip nat inside interface g1/2 ip nat outside
